title: Jagged Charred Mexican Pork Tamales
description: A charred, gooey, festive Mexican dish featuring freshly chopped parsley, katsuramuki-cut pork, and egg-free friendly ingredients, served in a molcajete vessel as tamales.
instructions: Soak the dried corn husks in water for 30 minutes to make them pliable.
In a large bowl, combine the masa harina and chicken broth, and stir until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it is smooth and pliable.
In a large skillet, heat the lard over medium heat, and cook the katsuramuki-cut pork shoulder until it is charred and cooked through.
Add the ancho chili powder and salt to the skillet, and stir to combine.
To assemble the tamales, lay a corn husk flat, and spread a thin layer of the dough onto the center of the husk.
Place a few pieces of the charred pork onto the center of the dough, and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Fold the sides of the corn husk over the filling, and then roll the tamale up, starting from the wide end.
Repeat the process until all of the ingredients are used up.
Place the tamales in a large steamer basket, and steam over boiling water for 45 minutes.
Serve the tamales in a molcajete vessel, garnished with additional chopped parsley if desired.
